text:
maria: FYI support ticket from Acme: they got a 429 on production at ~2026-03-12T11:02Z even though the project dashboard shows ~200k remaining tokens for the day. Customer says this started after a recent spike. ticket: https://zendesk.example/12345

support-bot: created ticket #12345 for Acme — assigned to @maria :white_check_mark:

jonah: invoice shows 1,200,345 tokens billed for the day, but project dashboard shows ~800k total used. billing->metering mismatch?

maria: exact customer repro: they hit this endpoint in a tight loop (low concurrency):
```bash
for i in {1..120}; do \
  curl -s -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
    -d '{"input":"short prompt"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate | tail -n 5
done
```
last response headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
X-Request-Id: rq_01F8...
X-RateLimit-Limit: 60000
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Window-Reset: 1768504380
```
customer says they only sent ~120 requests (~40k tokens) not close to daily quota.

alex: :eyes: can you paste the request-id from one of the 429s and the project id? also, do we have the rate-limiter logs for that minute?

maria: request id rq_01F8ABCD. Project: acme-prod (proj_980). attaching a short excerpt from proxy logs (sanitized):
```
[11:01:59.123] req=rq_01F8ABCD project=proj_980 tokens=334 status=200
[11:02:05.421] req=rq_01F8ABCE project=proj_980 tokens=329 status=200
[11:02:12.009] req=rq_01F8ABCF project=proj_980 tokens=332 status=429
```

alex: quick theory: enforcement uses a rolling-window token counter in the rate-limiter service while the dashboard reads aggregated metering tables that are updated asynchronously (1–2 min delay). two possibilities: 1) a different pipeline is incrementing the same project's usage (embedding ingestion job?), or 2) enforcement has a separate cache and double-counted due to a race on window boundary.

sophie: adding eng-platform to triage. will check if embedding pipeline writes to the same metering top-level counter. also check if org-level pooling is enabled for acme (that can shift counts between projects).

jonah: for billing side: if metering writes are delayed, invoices will still include all tokens because billing job reads raw event stream. that explains invoices > dashboard. but doesn't explain immediate 429s.

alex: can we reproduce quickly with a synthetic load that mimics their pattern? if enforcement is using a token-based burst bucket, a burst of many small requests could exhaust the bucket though daily allowance remains. run this against a staging rate-limiter with the same config:
```bash
wrk -t2 -c4 -d10s -s scripts/spam_requests.lua -- /v1/generate?project=proj_980
```
watch the limiter service logs for bucket updates and for any negative deltas.

maria: customer wants a mitigation they can apply now. suggested options: 1) apply a temporary higher per-project soft limit, 2) enable org-fallback so project falls back to org quota, 3) advise to add client-side jitter to avoid synchronized bursts.

alex: agree. i'll patch a temporary soft-limit increase for proj_980 and enable org-fallback if their org quota covers it. also will tail limiter logs for the 11:02 window and dump the token counter state. if we see double-counting we need immediate rollback of the recent limiter change.

sophie: I found one suspicious entry in platform audit: an embedding backfill job started for acme at 11:00 and used a different ingestion path that increments metering via the ingestion-api and also emits a duplicate event to the event-stream. possible duplicate increments before dedupe runs.

jonah: note for customer messaging: explain that 429s were caused by temporary burst enforcement and that billing shows all events (including backfill). propose the short-term mitigation and say we are investigating duplication in the ingestion pipeline.

maria: I'll send the suggested message and offer the soft-limit bump. tagging @alex @sophie to confirm once the limiter dump and audit correlate.

alex: dumping limiter state now, attaching snippet: 
```
limiter:proj_980:window=1768504320 count=59812 last_inc=11:02:12
limiter:proj_980:window=1768504380 count=60001 last_inc=11:02:12 (threshold reached)
```
looks like two windows overlapped during the backfill spike and the enforcement cache saw counts > threshold briefly. root cause: ingestion job duplicate events + rolling-window edge.

sophie: will add a dedupe filter in the ingestion pipeline and add a small GC window on the limiter cache to avoid double-inc on window boundary. I'll open a PR and link it here.

maria: customer updated: they accepted the soft-limit bump and are pausing the backfill for now. thanks team. :tada:

alex: once PR is merged we should run a replay of the backfill in staging and monitor meters vs enforcement. if clean, we'll coordinate a patch deploy to production with a careful rollback plan.

maria: closing the support ticket after prod patch and a confirmation from billing that invoice numbers remain consistent. I'll follow up with customer post-mitigation. :white_check_mark:
